problem: A failed workspace chunk destroys the entire app
evidence: Blocking CurriculumLibrary-mMemtMU4.js produced a dynamic-import error, empty body text, zero main regions and zero retry buttons.
root: Suspense handles loading but the workspace lazy renderer has no surrounding error boundary. The scene-specific boundary does not cover these imports.
impact: A recoverable download problem removes navigation and all useful content.
fix: Keep the shell mounted; contain workspace failures and offer retry/reload and a route to another lab.
acceptance: Abort a lazy JS request; shell and accessible error status remain, retry/reload is operable, and another lab can open.

problem: Responsive mathematics shrinks below readable size
evidence: At 320px, neuron weight labels have an effective SVG font size of 4.97px, node values 7.87px and timeline labels 8px. Output begins at y=2088px.
root: A fixed 700-unit SVG is scaled into a 290px area; the layout treats fitting as usability.
impact: Students cannot comfortably read the numbers needed to reason about the model.
fix: Use a compact staged graph with readable HTML values, selected-edge detail beside controls, and optional pan/zoom for the full network.
acceptance: At 320/390/768px, essential mathematical labels have a readable equivalent at least 12px; selected parameter and resulting value can be compared without scrolling multiple screens.

problem: The first learning task is buried behind administration and explanation
evidence: At 320px the Your prediction label begins at y=2344px; the full first lesson is 6434px tall. Topic navigation has a 338px viewport around 4803px of content.
root: Evidence caveats, topic navigation, vocabulary and every support activity are composed as one mandatory vertical document.
impact: New learners scroll through instructions before doing the exercise and lose the task when opening support activities.
fix: Lead with one objective and prediction workspace; disclose vocabulary, evidence policy, recall, explanation and mixed review at their relevant moments.
acceptance: At 320px a learner reaches the first editable prediction within two initial viewports; recall and review remain discoverable and keyboard usable, and existing assessment gates remain intact.

problem: The modal allows background navigation
evidence: With the drawer open, clicking My learning changes to dashboard while the dialog stays visible; header has no inert attribute and focus moves to MAIN outside the dialog.
root: The scrim excludes the header; focus containment only wraps first/last elements and background controls remain active.
impact: The declared modal state disagrees with real interaction and focus behavior.
fix: Make non-dialog content inert while open, or redesign the navigation as a nonmodal drawer with correct semantics; preserve Escape and restoration.
acceptance: While a modal drawer is open, mouse, touch and keyboard cannot activate background controls; focus stays inside, Escape restores the trigger, and resizing closes cleanly.

problem: Leaving the mission discards the experiment recovery snapshot
evidence: Bias was 0.5, loading set it to -2; after navigating to dashboard and returning it remained -2, with zero Restore my experiment buttons and a fresh Load button.
root: Parameters live in Zustand while the saved prior experiment lives in a component that unmounts on navigation.
impact: Exploring another workspace silently removes the promised way to restore the learner's experiment.
fix: Give the mission transaction one owner with a lifecycle matching the lab, or restore explicitly on exit; retain the exact prior numeric configuration.
acceptance: Load mission, visit another workspace, return and restore original inputs, weights, bias and activation; correct/incorrect feedback and course-evidence isolation still pass.

problem: Three visual states fail text contrast
evidence: Selected tensor indices: 2.28:1 at 10px. Dimmed activation legends: 3.58:1 at 10px. CodeMirror red syntax: 4.08:1 on active line and 4.38:1 elsewhere at 14px. Expected minimum is 4.5:1 for this text.
root: Semantic selection fills, opacity dimming and editor syntax colors were not tested in their combined rendered states.
impact: Indices, curve identities and editable code are harder to read; the selected state can reduce legibility.
fix: Adjust foregrounds or selected fills and use contrast-safe inactive text; test editor token colors against both backgrounds.
acceptance: Axe contrast passes at desktop/mobile in selected tensor, all activation selections and active/inactive code lines; preserve mathematical color meanings.

problem: Interactive chart semantics and Space activation are broken
evidence: Axe flags the SVG role=img with focusable descendants. Space on Inspect layer 3 keeps Layer 1 selected; Enter selects Layer 3.
root: An interactive widget is exposed as a single image; custom role=button handles only Enter.
impact: Assistive technology can miss child controls and keyboard activation is inconsistent with buttons.
fix: Expose a grouped interactive chart with named controls supporting Enter and Space, and an equivalent textual layer selector.
acceptance: No nested-interactive violation; keyboard and assistive names identify each layer; Enter and Space select the same layer and update the exact inspector.

problem: Scrollable truth table lacks a keyboard focus entry
evidence: Axe flags .perceptron-table as scrollable-region-focusable at 390px.
root: Horizontal overflow is handled visually but the wrapper has no focusable content or focus target.
impact: Keyboard users cannot reliably inspect the offscreen result columns.
fix: Name and focus the scrolling region with a visible focus outline, or use a narrow-screen row disclosure preserving table relationships.
acceptance: At 320/390px keyboard users can reach and scroll every column; axe rule passes and header/value relationships remain understandable.

problem: ARIA tabs are ordinary buttons dressed as a tab widget
evidence: ArrowRight while Math is focused leaves focus and selection on Math. All tabs remain normal tab stops; source lacks linked tabpanel/aria-controls and tab keyboard handling.
root: Only tablist/tab roles and selected appearance were added, without the corresponding interaction contract.
impact: Keyboard and assistive-technology expectations do not match the widget.
fix: Implement linked tab panels and roving focus with arrow/Home/End handling, or use an honestly named button group.
acceptance: If tabs remain, arrow keys move between tabs, one tab is in the tab sequence, selected panel is named/linked and all content stays reachable.

problem: Deep navigation has no deep URL or history
evidence: Selecting Training diagnostics leaves #/lab/beginner unchanged; opening a chapter leaves #/lab/library unchanged. Workspace history works, nested lesson/document history is absent. Two authored CH-00 Python document files are not linked in the chapter reader; 87 other catalog entries are deliberately planned without separate Markdown documents.
root: The route model owns only the workspace; selection belongs to local state/storage.
impact: Students cannot share their exact lesson/document or reliably use Back between them; native open-in-new-tab is absent from sidebar button destinations.
fix: Extend the existing whitelist URL state to valid topic and document IDs; use anchors for real destinations while preserving storage fallback.
acceptance: Copy/reload an exact topic/document URL in a clean context; Back/Forward restores prior topic/document, invalid IDs fall back safely, native link actions work. Every available authored reference document has a discoverable link; planned catalog-only entries remain clearly labeled.

problem: Chapter detail opens after the entire catalog
evidence: At 768px the catalog starts 4909px tall; opening its first chapter scrolls to y=4298. At 320px the unfiltered catalog is 8849px tall.
root: The detail article is appended after all 19 chapter summaries, then the page scrolls to it.
impact: Opening the first item jumps far away from its context and returning requires a large scroll or filter reset.
fix: Use a persistent compact chapter index with adjacent desktop detail and a dedicated mobile detail state with explicit return-to-results.
acceptance: Open first/middle/last chapter without traversing other chapter content; return preserves query, chapter and scroll position; label implemented practice versus specifications.

problem: Review selection does not follow the selected lesson chapter
evidence: After switching from first topic to Training diagnostics, Review chapter remained value 0 (CH-00). The review starts at CH-00 on each component mount.
root: ChapterReview owns an independent default chapter and receives no current-chapter context.
impact: The bottom of a CH-07 lesson presents unrelated CH-00 review unless the learner notices and changes the selector.
fix: Offer the current chapter's review at its checkpoint, with an explicit option to choose another chapter.
acceptance: Selecting a lesson in each chapter presents the intended contextual review; deliberate cross-chapter selection remains available and persisted results retain their correct chapter identity.

problem: Practice disappears when moving between tools
evidence: These components own attempts/evidence in useState and say it lasts for the visit; authored beginner evidence and inference checkpoints persist. Reloading tools resets their transfer evidence by construction.
root: Sandbox practice, authored course progress and checkpoint persistence have separate contracts with no coherent learner handoff.
impact: A student can complete an experiment, leave to inspect a related concept and lose its transfer record. The labels are honest, but the workflow is fragmented.
fix: Decide which practice belongs to a saved draft/history; preserve provenance and distinguish exploratory attempts from course evidence without inventing mastery.
acceptance: A documented evidence contract survives reload/navigation for intended records, backups include them where appropriate, and exploratory actions never grant authored course credit.

problem: Primary, secondary and unavailable actions compete visually
evidence: Python flow initially shows five similarly styled execution/transport buttons. Neuron mixes inspect-node buttons, four transport buttons and six timeline buttons. Training's Cancel Python training is a native-style button outside the styled action group.
root: Styling follows container selectors instead of action importance; duplicate transport systems have different labels and grouping.
impact: The next meaningful action is harder to find and disabled controls take attention before there is a result to navigate.
fix: Define primary/secondary/quiet/danger controls; place playback near its visualization, and reveal result-only controls when usable.
acceptance: Each task has a visually dominant next action; cancellation looks consistent, transport remains keyboard accessible, and empty states explain why the task is not ready.

problem: The design system is an override layer over surviving feature dialects
evidence: styles.css has 593 rule blocks and workspace.css adds 276, with 17 total !important occurrences. Palette tokens coexist with literal green/amber chart colors and a gray One Dark editor.
root: Incremental restyling preserved old selectors and adds broad global overrides; shared palette migration is incomplete.
impact: A component's appearance depends on cascade order and feature context; local fixes can create cross-page inconsistencies.
fix: Consolidate one primitive at a time into explicit surface, action and chart roles; retire superseded rules only with comparison evidence.
acceptance: A migrated primitive has one owner, no competing legacy declaration and defined state colors; all five-width screenshots and relevant interactions remain valid.

problem: Several checks verify recognition after teaching the answer
evidence: Tensor asks rank 1 versus rank 10 while the same page explains rank counts axes. Activation asks ReLU versus Leaky ReLU at -2 after the graph/note exposes the behavior. Perceptron's XOR check offers Yes/No without an XOR experiment.
root: One reusable end-of-page binary-question pattern substitutes for topic-specific transfer tasks.
impact: Checks can support immediate feedback but provide weak evidence of independent understanding; no learner-outcome improvement is established.
fix: Preserve quick checks as orientation; add fresh predict-before-reveal tasks such as choosing a slice, diagnosing a saturated derivative, or attempting an XOR boundary.
acceptance: A new task requires a prediction/construction on unseen valid parameters, offers evidence-based feedback, and does not reveal its answer before submission or relabel existing checks as mastery.

problem: Plots are correct enough to compute but weakly equipped to be read
evidence: Gradient-depth says log-scaled but its vertical axis has no numerical tick values. The loss contour draws five unlabeled levels with direction text, no coordinate ticks or level legend.
root: Charts prioritize a clean illustration and an exact inspector without fully exposing their coordinate/scale contract.
impact: Students can inspect a selected value but cannot easily interpret magnitude or contour distance directly from the plot.
fix: Add readable axes/ticks, level labels and selected-point linkage; retain exact model values and disclose clipping/scales.
acceptance: At desktop/mobile a learner can identify axis variables, scale and contour/layer values from labels; mathematical levels and path still agree with the engine.

problem: Invalid values are silently replaced instead of explained
evidence: Filling B[1,1] with 999 leaves the input at its old value 2. No invalid-input message appears; deleting the input is converted through Number('') to 0.
root: The controlled input stores only accepted numeric values and discards the user's editing text.
impact: Learners cannot tell whether their input was accepted, rejected or changed, and transient editing states are awkward.
fix: Keep draft text separately, validate on an explicit boundary, and show an associated inline range/finite-number message.
acceptance: Blank, transient minus, out-of-range and nonfinite input states have understandable feedback; no silent computation with an unintended replacement value; valid values still update the matrix exactly.

problem: No-match search produces an unexplained blank region
evidence: Searching zzzz-no-match rendered zero glossary articles and an empty string, without a result count or no-results message.
root: The filter renders the map result directly without an empty-state/status branch.
impact: Students cannot distinguish no results from a failed display and receive no recovery suggestion.
fix: Provide an announced result count, no-results explanation and clear-filter action; consider compact results instead of all definitions by default.
acceptance: Zero and nonzero result states are announced without excessive chatter; clear filter restores all results and keyboard focus stays stable.

problem: Unrelated learning tasks keep the same visual rhythm
evidence: Foundation, tensor, activation, forward, backprop and loss repeat heading/eyebrow, two rounded workbench containers, smaller blue metric containers, binary check and source/code tail. Backprop's four derivative/update tiles resemble loss's five arithmetic tiles despite different teaching tasks.
root: Shared panel/metric patterns are applied more consistently than task-specific composition.
impact: Primary experimentation, supporting proof and reference material lose differentiation; familiarity becomes monotony rather than orientation.
fix: Keep a shared shell but compose around the learning operation: a trace ledger for backprop, a plot-and-step strip for optimization, and a row/column inspector for tensors. Use boxes for boundaries, not every number.
acceptance: Each lab has one identifiable primary interaction and subordinate supporting proof; existing controls/content remain available, and before/after evidence shows distinction without introducing new dependencies or layouts for their own sake.
